Kazi Akter Hamid with Salma Sultana and Sultana Parvin—For the Petitioners 
Md. Khurshid Alam Khan—For Respondent No. 4

Delwar Hossain (Md)and others ----- Petitioners
vs
Bangladesh represented by the Secretary Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Dhaka and others ----- Respondents.
full_judgment:
Mir Md. Joynal Abedin Shibly, Deputy Director, Durniti Daman Commission (the Commission, in brief), passed an order on 29-3-2010 to petitioner No. 1, Md. Delwar Hossain, under section 26(1) of the Durniti Daman Commission Ain, 2004 (hereinafter referred to as the Ain, 2004) by Memo No. দুদক/বিঃ অনুঃ ও তদন্ত-১/১২২-২০০৯/৫৩৮৫ to furnish details of the properties and sources of income of petitioner No. 1 and his wife, son and daughter i. e. his dependents within seven days. Petitioner No. 1, upon receiving the notice on 30-3-2010, submitted a written statements explaining his position, but the Commission refused to accept his explanation and it filed a criminal case being Bangladesh Police Station Case No. 40 dated 19-5-2010 under section 26(2)(ka) of the Ain, 2004 against petitioner No.1 for tailing to supply the details of his properties and sources of income. Thereafter, the Sub-Assistant (উপসহকারী) Director of the Commission submitted charge-sheet against petitioner No. 1 under section 26(2) of the Ain, 2004 on 25-8-2010. Petitioner No. 1 obtained anticipatory bail from High Court Division on 11-10-2010 in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 29199 of 2010. The said case is under trial before Special Tribunal No. 6, Dhaka. Mr. Md. Nazimuddin, Investigating Officer and Sub-Assistant (উপসহকারী) Director of the Commission, on 20-9-2010, issued a letter under Memo No. 17538(3) to the petitioners directing them to appear before him at the office of the Commission on 26-9-2010 and, on 30-9-2010, he issued another letter under Memo No. 18556 to the petitioners for sup-ply of some information/records for the purpose of enquiry. On 3-10-2010, the said person issued another letter under Memo No. 18579 to petitioner No. 1 for inspection of his Flat and for measurement thereof by an Engineer. Whereupon, petitioner No. 1 filed Writ Petition No. 8501 of 2010 challenging the letters issued under the signature of Mr. Md. Nazimuddin and a Rule Nisi was issued in the said writ petition. During pendency of the Rule, the Commission lodged an FIR with Paltan Police Station against the petitioners being Paltan Police Station Case No. 9 dated 4-5-2011. No investigation report has yet been submitted in connection with the said case. The petitioners were enlarged on anticipatory bail in the said case in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 18082 of 2011 on 22-6-2011 by the High Court Division. On 9-6-2011, respondent No. 5, the investigating officer of Paltan Police Station Case No. 9 dated 4-5-2011, filed an application before the Metropolitan Session Judge, Dhaka for seizure of the records of accounts and also to freeze bank/financial institutions accounts of the petitioners as described in the said petition. Thereafter, on 12-6-2011, respondent No. 3, the Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka issued a letter to respondent No. 5 according permission to seize records of accounts and also to freeze bank/financial institutions accounts of the petitioners as described in the petition dated 9-6-2011. 

 5. Mr. Kazi Akter Hamid, the learned Advocate for the petitioners, takes us through the writ petition and the connected materials on record as well as the impugned order and submits that from the application dated 9-6-2011 filed by respondent No. 5, the investigating officer of Paltan Police Station Case No. 9 dated 4-5-2011, it appears that the said application was filed for seizure of some documents from banks and other financial institutions under section 94(1)(ka) of the CrPC and also to freeze the bank/financial institutions accounts of the petitioners. He next submits that on receiving the application, the Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka unlawfully passed the impugned order under Memo No. DMSJ /74(1)/C dated 12-6-2011 giving permission to seize records and freeze the bank/financial institutions accounts of the petitioners under section 94(1 )(ka) of the CrPC from the banks and financial institutions as mentioned in the impugned order. He further submits that under section 18 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007 (hereinafter stated as the Rules), the Metropolitan Sessions Judge had/has no jurisdiction to permit the investigating officer to freeze accounts or to seize documents of the petitioners for the purpose of enquiry/investigation relating to anti-corruption matters and the matter is absolutely within the domain of the Special Judge of the relevant jurisdiction. He finally submits that under section 94(1)(ka) of the CrPC the Metropolitan Session Judge has no jurisdiction to pass any order relating to seizure of documents or freeze of accounts during investigation of a case by the Commission and therefore, the impugned order is liable to be struck down. 

 8. On careful study of the aforesaid provisions of laws, it is evident that an application to freeze or seize documents, etc. during investigation of a case by the Commission has to be made before the Special Judge having jurisdiction over the properties and the Special Judge has exclusive jurisdiction to accord permission to seize documents or freeze bank/financial institutions accounts under rule 18 of the Rules and that under section 94(1 )(ka) of the CrPC, the Metropolitan Sessions Judge has no jurisdiction to give permission to seize documents or freeze accounts relating to investigation etc. of anti-corruption cases. The learned Advocate for the Commission also admits the said legal proposition.
